subject: Inde-Navarrette
research_tasks: Quote fidelity: every video quote below comes from YouTube auto-captions. Verify against audio before quoting. Known caption errors: 'Karyn'/'Korean' = Curry (Barker), 'Superstore' = Superman & Lois, 'Obsessed' = Obsession, 'India Eisley'/'Indian Naidu' = Inde Navarrette.

Web-article quotes were retrieved through a summarizing fetch tool. Re-open Nylon, Complex, Mixed Feelings, Numero, CBR 2021, Looper 2022, KryptonSite 2023, Just Jared Jr 2023 and the Seventeen/Yahoo copy and match wording verbatim before quoting.

Hot Ones Versus (S12) transcript has no speaker labels. Confirm on video which of Navarrette or Michael Johnston says the lines at 02:21 ('Sometimes I just get anxious'), 04:57 ('the one thing I can control is taking off my jacket') and 12:09 ('do my parents proud'). They were deliberately left out of the claims until attributed. The S13 testimony lines (14:33-14:45, 15:22-15:31) are attributed from context and also need a visual check.
Alamo Drafthouse Q&A (S16) 15:16 'That was her idea, and it was brilliant' has no speaker label (probably Barker). Confirm before attributing to Barker.

Birth date: March 3, 2001 appears only in third-party profiles (S01, S05). She confirms first name Danielle (S11 21:25) and 'I just turned 25' (S14, June 2026). If no primary source for the exact day is found, use 'March 2001' or '2001'.
'Eleven schools by age fifteen' is sourced only to Wikipedia/HOLA. Find the original interview or attribute it to reporting. She herself says she 'grew up moving around a lot' (S10).
Sibling count conflicts: she says 'second oldest of seven... six or seven... split families' (S10); Wikipedia lists four siblings. Prefer 'second-oldest in a large blended family'.
Gladiator age conflicts: 'like five' (S09) vs 'like three' (S10). Use 'as a small child'.
Budget conflicts: $750,000 (NBC News, Wikipedia via Deadline) vs $1,000,000 (The Numbers). Say 'about $750,000' with attribution, or 'under $1 million'.

Relationship: as of 2026-09-10 coverage of musician Nick Aiello is paparazzi/rumor-level (Just Jared, SCMP 'rumoured'); she has not confirmed it in any source opened here. Do not state relationship status in body or FAQs.

Critical-review quotes (Variety/Guy Lodge, Vulture/Louis Peitzman, /Film) and the 2026 award wins were seen only via Wikipedia (S01). Open the reviews (try Yahoo/AOL syndications, since Variety/THR/GoldDerby hit tollbit) or cite the award bodies before using them.

Superman & Lois 2023 contemporaneous reaction: the TikTok quote ('at least we got a Season 4') is known only from a search snippet (S32, Cinemablend truncated). Open the Cinemablend article or the TikTok, or rely only on the 2026 Collider retrospective (S09) and label it hindsight.

Time-sensitive checks before publish: Obsession worldwide gross (S27), X-Men (2028) casting and release date (S24), the SNL hosting date of 2026-10-31 (S26). After Oct 31, 2026, confirm the SNL episode aired.
Deadline (2026-08-31) reports an Obsession executive producer suing over profits. It does not involve Navarrette; do not reference or imply her involvement.

Sensitive: CBR 2021 (S19) has her saying she 'very personally' has an attachment to what her character Sarah went through (a mental-health and suicide-attempt arc). Do not infer a diagnosis, attempt or causal wound. Quote only her words, or omit.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette
sources.speaker: Wikipedia contributors
sources.locator: Early life; Career; Personal life; Accolades sections
sources.excerpt: Born March 3, 2001, in Tucson, Arizona... born Danielle Fabiola Navarrette... father of Mexican heritage, U.S. Marine Corps veteran; mother an Australian hairstylist... by age fifteen had attended eleven schools... Superman & Lois (2021-2024)... departed along with six costars due to budget cuts in June 2023... cast as Rogue in untitled X-Men film (2028)... scheduled to host Saturday Night Live on October 31, 2026.
sources.context: Tertiary compilation. Useful for timeline and pointers to citations; not independent corroboration. Critical-reception quotes and the awards table in this article were not traced to their original outlets.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette Wants To Prove 'Obsession' Isn't Just "Lightning In A Bottle"
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Lauren McCarthy (Nylon)
sources.locator: Brunch-at-Carnegie-Deli profile; paragraphs on auditions, fame and privacy
sources.excerpt: Between Obsession and the film after that, I didn't work. I was walking dogs. I was streaming. I was doing a lot of these things to make money. I didn't have a lot of confidence because you just keep hearing no, and that can be debilitating. / I don't care how much I'm not sleeping, because I don't know if I'll get this opportunity again. / I really want to prove that Obsession wasn't just lightning in a bottle... I also want to fall on my face publicly and have something that people don't like [but] maybe I do. / I already have that as a girl... I just clock it. I don't want it to affect the way that I go about things, but I'm a very private person.
sources.context: In-person profile about two months after release. The writer frames the privacy quote as being about unsolicited public attention; the not-sleeping quote follows a paragraph about strangers stopping her and her Instagram reaching 2.2 million followers. She laughs after the fall-on-my-face line.

sources.title: In Conversation With Inde Navarrette
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Jana Letonja; written by Anouk Woudt (Numero Netherlands)
sources.date: May 13 (year not displayed; content dates it to 2026)
sources.locator: Q&A: 'What drew you to the project?', 'How did working within the horror genre challenge you?', 'How does Obsession represent a turning point?'
sources.excerpt: I really wanted to transition into film, but to do it in a way that showed more of what I was capable as an actress. / My approach to that was fully submitting to the fact that the character I was playing had no control. / Horror was something I never thought I would be a part of. I am so deeply afraid of horror. / The first time that I felt like I wasn't part of someone else's story. Obsession is Nikki.
sources.context: Release-week press Q&A. The 'no control' line is about playing Nikki, not a self-description; do not use it as evidence of her own control needs.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette Desperately Seeks Someone to Nerd Out With
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Logan (mixed feelings Substack)
sources.locator: Hyperspecific questionnaire; nickname and family passages
sources.excerpt: I would always say, 'Mommy, I do.' That's how I got my nickname, Inde, because I was very independent. / She's a hairstylist and I would tell her clients that I don't let her do my hair. So very 'I do.' / I remember going with my stepmom to watch New Moon... it was our first time bonding. / I want to direct one day.
sources.context: Fan-culture questionnaire (anime, Kingdom Hearts, Twilight). Her mother's reported reply: 'Okay. You're my first daughter. I would like to dress you.' Nickname story is her retrospective self-report.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette on Struggling to Book Roles After Filming 'Obsession': 'Nothing Was Sticking'
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Jillian Superstar (Complex News); written by Alex Ocho
sources.locator: Article body quoting the Complex News video interview
sources.excerpt: I was auditioning, I was doing everything, just nothing was sticking. I wanted to pay rent and I wanted to do things. So I was walking dogs, I was streaming, doing everything I could. / I think I was in a space personally where I was so shut off from my own emotions, and with Nikki, you need all of them. / If I have this opportunity, I'm doing everything that I possibly can.
sources.context: The 'shut off' line describes her state at the Zoom callback; the 'opportunity' line describes her mindset going into the chemistry read. She also says of streaming: 'I'm doing this by myself in my room. Why don't I try?'

sources.title: Inde Navarrette couldn't get a job for one and a half years after 'Obsession' wrapped
sources.speaker: Victoria Luxford (NME), quoting Complex
sources.locator: Article body
sources.excerpt: I didn't work for a year and a half after Obsession... The audition process for Obsession was so crazy. I sent in a tape, they liked it, I went in for a Zoom read, it was awful.
sources.context: Rewrite of the Complex interview (S06); not independent corroboration. Retained only for the 'it was awful' line and the year-and-a-half figure.

sources.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Explains What's Really Happening to Nikki (Collider Ladies Night)
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Perri Nemiroff
sources.locator: Timestamps: 01:33-02:25 (audition high/low), 04:36-05:07 (Gladiator), 06:00-06:22 (mom's advice), 08:07-08:45 (Superman & Lois as college), 09:45-10:23 (leaving the show), 11:20-11:46 (Cudlitz), 14:34-15:21 (felt seen), 20:24-21:35 (shyness, scream), 25:02-25:31 (alternate ending), 28:46-29:12 (proud of)
sources.excerpt: Honestly, I kind of felt like it was a blessing, not necessarily in disguise, but kind of just right in front of my face... as soon as they were kind of like, 'Dog, you're free.' I was like, 'Dude.'... So, that was hard to hear cuz I miss everybody... I got freedom. And it was again, to treat it like college, like I graduated. / Whenever I met [Curry and] everybody, I was in a really shy place in my life... I said, 'I don't know how to scream, and I'm feeling very shy.' / my mom really instilled in me to um not take no until no's a for sure.
sources.context: 30-minute spoiler interview on release weekend. Nemiroff frames the Superman & Lois exit as budget-driven before asking. Retrospective after Obsession's success, so the 'blessing' reframe carries hindsight. Auto-caption renders Curry as 'Karyn'.

sources.title: 'Obsession's Inde Navarrette on Fame, X-Men, Oscar Buzz, & What Video Games She's Playing (Up Next with Variety)
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Tiana (Variety)
sources.locator: Timestamps: 01:03-01:58 (rescued cat), 04:26-05:17 (Schreier, Mystique), 05:46-07:22 (family, moving), 07:27-08:57 (strict Marine dad, hit by a car, college), 10:33-11:23 (deleted Twitch streams), 11:41-12:44 (streaming origins), 14:30-16:05 (discerning, audience trust), 19:04-19:22 (his vision), 19:56-22:33 (fame, 'none of my business'), 23:53-24:46 (left high school early), 25:24-27:07 (Mommy I do, place to hide, standing up), 27:17-28:24 (things I can control), 28:30-29:41 (Oscar safety net), 30:06-30:24 (sensitive to horror), 31:40-31:48 (test the waters)
sources.excerpt: Oh, I like I deleted all of them just cuz I felt like I was I got scared and I was like, why moving into like a new chapter of my life? Like what if people saw that I switched and now they don't take me seriously or it was just a lot of I mean it's not based on fact, but it I just panicked and I deleted a lot of them... now seeing that people are so lovingly holding on to it my fear was for nothing. / whenever it comes to what I do have control over in order to keep myself secure um it'll be my drives. It'll be my music. It'll be my video games / there's a part of my brain that is um just kind of having a safety net of if it doesn't happen, it doesn't mean that I didn't do a good job / Me, I was like new story, new place. / I don't think that far ahead.
sources.context: 33-minute solo podcast, the longest single-subject source. Speaker attribution is unambiguous (one guest). Host opens by misreading her name ('India Eisley' in captions). The Twitch answer responds to 'Are the streams still up on Twitch?'

sources.title: Inde Navarrette on 'Obsession' Oscar dreams, freaky stories, what happens to Nikki after the credits (GoldDerby Awards Magnet)
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Ethan Alter (GoldDerby)
sources.locator: Timestamps: 03:00-04:10 (boiling pot, worst audition), 05:12-05:34 (kept Nikki private), 09:21-09:31 (if that's what Curry said), 17:56-18:30 (sensitive, Curry as mirror), 21:09-21:40 (torn ACL, 'Danielle, hold it together'), 30:16-30:20 (off social media), 31:01-31:09 (shameful emotions), 32:02-32:15 (validating), 35:48-36:47 (chasing that high, be stubborn)
sources.excerpt: I felt like I was a boiling pot that kept like as soon as steam would come out I kept being taken off the stove and I really wanted to like blow off some steam / I just needed to keep her private. I've really kept Nikki close to my chest. And so on that first day, Curry talks about how relieved he felt / I'm quite sensitive and so I didn't want to take anything home. So, I kind of used Curry as a mirror where I put full trust in him / Kind of chasing that high to challenge myself. I think obviously whenever you're really scared of something, but you really want to do it justice and do it correctly and then you get that high of uh accomplishing it and feeling proud of it. / be extremely stubborn, you know what I mean? Kind of be delusional a little bit. You have to really believe in yourself before other people will.
sources.context: 37-minute awards-campaign podcast. Incentive to present as serious and humble. The 'Curry relieved' detail is her account of what Barker says, not Barker's own words.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette vs. Michael Johnston | Hot Ones Versus
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette and Michael Johnston (First We Feast)
sources.locator: Timestamp 17:22-17:31 (charades origin story)
sources.excerpt: The beginning of 'Obsession' was charades, because I was too scared to do shit, and Curry was like, 'You got to get over that,' and he's like, 'You're all going to come over and play charades.'
sources.context: Comedic hot-wing game show; stress and bravado are part of the format. Transcript has no speaker labels. This line is attributed to Navarrette because it repeats her Collider account (S09 20:24-21:35) in the first person.

sources.title: Inde Navarrette vs. Michael Johnston | Hot Ones Versus (Johnston's remarks)
sources.speaker: Michael Johnston (Obsession co-star)

And you were like, 'No.' You were like, 'No.' / Dude, and guess who always answers the phone? Every time I call, you always answer me... You have never not answered the phone. I love this girl.

sources.title: 'Obsession' SPOILER Interviews with Curry Barker, Inde Navarrette and Michael Johnston (CinemaBlend)
sources.speaker: Curry Barker (writer-director)
sources.locator: Timestamp 03:17-04:13
sources.excerpt: What she really brought that I really appreciated was she she brought she brought um a personality trait to the real Nikki that I did not anticipate... what Indy brought was this like bro-y type of uh uh like um sassiness to Nikki that I didn't anticipate, but ended up working really well for the movie. Because it kind of emphasizes that Bear is totally in the friend zone.
sources.context: Director testimony in a joint press junket. Barker had written Nikki as a 'really sweet girl next door'. He also says he showed her films 'that it wasn't'.

sources.title: OBSESSION Q&A w/ Curry Barker, Inde Navarette, Michael Johnston, Cooper Tomlinson, Megan Lawless (Alamo Drafthouse)
sources.speaker: Curry Barker and Inde Navarrette (panel)
sources.locator: Timestamps: 15:02-16:22 (not-perceived idea; 'up to me to make myself comfortable'), 22:55-23:37 (Barker on the ending)
sources.excerpt: Barker: Capstone really wants us to do a version where you live, so we're just going to do one one take... Her performance was so crazy with the with the take where she lives, and so disturbing, um that I had people basically talk me into it and be like, 'She has to live, dude. It's way crazier if she lives.' / Navarrette: But there's some moments where it's just up to me to make myself comfortable.
sources.context: Post-screening panel. Barker's account of why the ending changed (studio-requested throwaway take, persuaded by her performance) differs in emphasis from hers in S09 (decided on the day: 'she's a final girl'). An unlabeled panelist, probably Barker, says of the not-perceived idea 'That was her idea, and it was brilliant.'

sources.title: TIFF 2025 Interview: Curry Barker on Crushing It in 'Obsession'
sources.speaker: Curry Barker, interviewed by Stephen Saito (Moveable Fest)
sources.locator: Answer to 'What sold you on Inde and Michael to play these characters?'
sources.excerpt: It was a really hard casting process because I was going for super-natural... some people were really good at the scary stuff, but they couldn't get the crazy stuff quite right, or they were really good at the crazy stuff, but they couldn't get the natural stuff quite right and that was a journey to find someone that could nail both those worlds, and Inde just nailed it.
sources.context: Pre-release festival interview, before the box-office run; the earliest director testimony and the least shaped by later success.

sources.title: Superman & Lois Interview: Inde Navarrette on Sarah Cushing
sources.speaker: Inde Navarrette, interviewed by Meagan Damore (CBR)
sources.locator: Q&A on background, audition process and character
sources.excerpt: I love to think of myself as a very strong woman. / I'm going to give it 110%. / My gut intuition was just like, 'You got it.' / I've been so fortunate and unfortunate to very personally have an attachment to what Sarah has gone through. / I love people, I love talking, I love being with friends.
sources.context: Pre-fame (series premiere) interview. She describes working with her mother on an audition and rejection mindset from age 13, writing down astrology signs 'from Aries all the way to Pisces' to keep focus at a screen test, auditions as 'survival mode', and calling herself 'very private'. Retrieved via summarizing fetch; verify wording.

claims.claim: She was born Danielle Fabiola Navarrette in Tucson, Arizona, in March 2001 (profiles give March 3, 2001).
claims.inference: First name is corroborated by her own self-address on set ('Danielle, hold it together', S11 21:25). Age is consistent with 'I just turned 25' in June 2026 (S14). The exact day appears only in third-party profiles.
claims.alternative: If no primary source for March 3 is found, publish 'March 2001' only.

claims.claim: Her father is a Mexican-American U.S. Marine and her mother an Australian hairstylist who built her own business. Her parents divorced, and her mother raised the children mostly in California's Central Valley (Visalia, Fresno, Bakersfield area).
claims.inference: Her own words: 'My dad's a Marine' (S10 06:10), 'She built her own business' (S10 08:52), 'she's a hairstylist' (S04), 'the Australian side... the Mexican side' (S14 07:04). Where her father was born is not established; 'Mexican heritage' is the safe phrasing.
claims.alternative: None material. Avoid characterizing the divorce beyond her statement.

claims.claim: Because of her father's service the family moved often, and she says she liked it: other military kids hated moving, but for her it was 'new story, new place'.
claims.inference: Retrospective self-report (S10 06:22-06:50). She adds that as an adult she has come to appreciate 'a small town mentality'. It shows novelty-tolerance in childhood.
claims.alternative: Counterevidence to a security-seeking reading. It fits Type 7 novelty-seeking, or simple adaptability, and may be a rosy retelling.

claims.claim: Reports say she had attended eleven schools by age fifteen.
claims.inference: Plausible given her account of frequent military moves, but no primary interview for the number was located.
claims.alternative: The figure may be inflated or garbled in aggregation. Attribute to reporting or omit.

claims.claim: She describes herself as the second-oldest in a large blended family ('second oldest of seven... six or seven... split families'); Wikipedia lists four siblings.
claims.inference: The discrepancy likely reflects step- and half-siblings across two households. Her mention of a stepmom (S04) fits that.
claims.alternative: Use 'a large blended family' and avoid a specific count.

claims.claim: Her nickname came from a childhood habit of insisting 'Mommy, I do': refusing to let her hairstylist mother do her hair or blow her bubbles.
claims.inference: An early, repeated insistence on doing things herself. In the Variety telling (S10 25:32-25:36) she attaches 'Mommy, I do. Like I do' to watching Gladiator and wanting to act, so the phrase carries both meanings in her retelling.
claims.alternative: A family origin story told in a light press context. Childhood autonomy-insistence is common and does not discriminate between types (it fits 6 counterphobic, 7 or 8).

claims.claim: She decided to act as a small child after watching Russell Crowe in Gladiator, and her mother overheard her reciting monologues from it.
claims.inference: Stable early vocation. She gives her age as 'like five' (S09 04:36) and 'like three' (S10 25:24).
claims.alternative: The age is inconsistent; use 'as a small child'.

claims.claim: Her mother taught her persistence ('not take no until no's a for sure'), worked with her on a rejection mindset from age 13, and drove her to Los Angeles auditions.
claims.inference: Across 2021 (S19) and 2026 (S09) she credits a parent-installed script for rejection. That suggests persistence learned inside a trusted relationship.
claims.alternative: A standard stage-parent narrative; it establishes influence, not motive.

claims.claim: She left high school early to work at a coffee shop because headshots were expensive and her mother couldn't afford them, then worked gym sales at Orangetheory and in a restaurant kitchen.
claims.inference: A costly early choice that put the acting goal ahead of a conventional path. Her Marine father 'really really loves to push education' (S10 07:33-07:40), so the choice carried family friction she mentions only lightly.
claims.alternative: Wikipedia lists Mt. Whitney and Redondo Union high schools. 'Left early' does not specify whether she finished by another route. Don't state 'dropped out'.

claims.claim: Early credits: Snapchat's Denton's Death Date (2019), Estela de la Cruz in 13 Reasons Why season 4 (2020), and Sarah Cortez/Cushing in The CW's Superman & Lois (2021-2024), where she was a series regular for three seasons before 2023 budget cuts reduced her to guest appearances.
claims.inference: Established filmography. The budget reason is the interviewer's framing in S09 and Wikipedia's account.
claims.alternative: Character surname varies by source (Cortez/Cushing). Check the show's credits and use one consistently.

claims.claim: She calls Superman & Lois her 'college': after she was hit by a car during production and couldn't walk between takes, she sat beside the cinematographers asking about lenses. She also stayed after work to watch Michael Cudlitz's scenes.
claims.inference: Turns a constraint into structured learning. She ties it explicitly to her father's emphasis on education and 'never stop learning' (S10 08:45-08:52), a way to meet a parental standard by another route.
claims.alternative: A common actor 'set was my film school' narrative; also compatible with Type 5 or 7 curiosity. The accident details are only her account.

claims.claim: In 2026 she described losing her series-regular role as 'a blessing... right in front of my face', and the producers as saying, in effect, 'Dog, you're free', while adding that it 'was hard to hear' because she missed the cast.
claims.inference: Quick positive reframing of a loss, told with hindsight after Obsession's success. The contemporaneous 2023 reaction (S32) was not opened.
claims.alternative: A Type 7 marker (reframe toward freedom and options). Could also be a public-relations-safe retelling. Treat as evidence for the alternative type rather than the thesis.

claims.claim: In 2023, while the show's renewal was uncertain, she treated an apparent green light cautiously: 'in our industry, it's not a definitive, so we still have to wait for that answer.'
claims.inference: A pre-fame, contemporaneous instance of withholding certainty until it's confirmed. A small but independent-in-time data point for a security-first reading.
claims.alternative: Ordinary industry realism, which any working actor would voice. Weak on its own.

claims.claim: Between wrapping Obsession and its release she went about a year and a half without acting work, walking dogs and streaming video games (on a PC she built) to pay rent. She said hearing 'no' repeatedly 'can be debilitating'.
claims.inference: Establishes the cost and constraint behind the breakout. The same story appears in several outlets, so it is consistent, but it is all self-report.
claims.alternative: None material. The 'year and a half' figure is hers.

claims.claim: She deleted most of her Twitch streams when she moved into acting because 'what if people saw that I switched and now they don't take me seriously', admitting 'it's not based on fact, but... I just panicked'. Later, seeing fans preserve the clips, she concluded 'my fear was for nothing'.
claims.inference: Central discriminator. Facing an imagined future judgment, she acted pre-emptively and at a cost, destroying an archive of something she 'love love loved' that had helped pay rent, and she names the act as fear-driven. That matches a security/anticipation motive more closely than 7 (keep the fun, move on), 4 (curate identity) or 3 (polish, not panic).
claims.alternative: A Type 3 image-management reading: protecting professional credibility. Against that, she volunteers the panic and calls the fear baseless on a Variety podcast, which a polish-first 3 is less likely to do. One retrospective episode, told lightly.

claims.claim: Her Zoom callback for Obsession went badly ('awful'; 'the worst audition I had ever done'). She says she was 'so shut off from my own emotions' then, and went into the chemistry read resolved: 'If I have this opportunity, I'm doing everything that I possibly can.'
claims.inference: A pattern of a shut-down, fearful baseline followed by a decisive push when one last chance appears. She also recalls deciding at the chemistry read to make Cooper Tomlinson 'utterly uncomfortable' (S09 13:27-14:15).
claims.alternative: A classic comeback-audition story shaped for press; fits many types.

claims.claim: Before Obsession she felt like 'a boiling pot' that kept being 'taken off the stove' as soon as steam came out, and she wanted a role that let her 'blow off some steam'.
claims.inference: Her own image of pent-up expression that circumstances kept interrupting. It ties to 'you're constantly told, No, don't show that' (S09 15:10) and the Nikki role as release.
claims.alternative: Supports Type 9 (self-suppression) or Type 4 (unexpressed inner life) as much as 6. Also an actor's metaphor about being typecast in small TV roles.

claims.claim: She arrived on Obsession 'in a really shy place' and didn't know how to scream. She told Barker so, and he scheduled private sessions and a cast charades game to get her past it ('I was too scared to do shit').
claims.inference: Consistent across two separate appearances (May and September 2026). Her response to fear is to disclose it to a trusted authority and accept a structured, graduated exposure. That fits a counterphobic 6 who needs a safe container before charging in.
claims.alternative: Ordinary performance nerves handled by a good director. Shyness also fits 4, 5 or 9.

claims.claim: She says she has been 'so sensitive' all her life, 'especially towards horror movies' ('I am so deeply afraid of horror'), yet took a horror lead. She credits the film with 'heal[ing] that' and calls the horror community 'the most welcoming... I don't ever want to leave that.'
claims.inference: Moving toward the feared genre, then attaching to the community that received her. That is fear, approach, then belonging. Tension: her Mexican family had Chucky on when she was about five (S14 07:21-07:35), so the fear coexisted with early exposure.
claims.alternative: Press-cycle gratitude toward a fan base; 'afraid of horror' is also a common junket line.

claims.claim: She describes a deliberate loop of seeking out what scares her: 'Kind of chasing that high to challenge myself... whenever you're really scared of something, but you really want to do it justice... you get that high of accomplishing it and feeling proud of it.' She credits the attitude to her parents.
claims.inference: Her own statement of a counterphobic motive: the reward is fear mastered, not novelty alone. It echoes 2021 ('I often challenge myself daily', S19) and the audition 'high... dopamine' (S09 01:45-01:57).
claims.alternative: Type 7 reading: the 'high' language points to stimulation-seeking. Type 3 reading: the payoff is pride. The discriminator is that she names fear as the entry condition, not options or image.

claims.claim: She kept her Nikki choices private from the cast and crew ('I've really kept Nikki close to my chest'), and says Barker has described being relieved on the first day when he saw what she could do.
claims.inference: Protects inner preparation from exposure until it is ready. The Barker 'relieved' line is her report of his words, not his own.
claims.alternative: A common actor technique for keeping reactions fresh. Fits Type 4/5 privacy as well as 6.

claims.claim: Co-star Michael Johnston recalls asking her to show him the 'freaky Nikki' smile in advance and her refusing, and says she has 'never not answered the phone' when he calls.
claims.inference: Second-person corroboration of the privacy-in-preparation claim (C21) and a small loyalty/reliability signal. Johnston elsewhere says 'she had that from the jump' (S18). Friendly, promotional context.
claims.alternative: Co-star praise in joint promotion is not independent of the press cycle. Speaker attribution in S13 is inferred and needs visual confirmation.

claims.claim: She describes deferring to Barker: 'I'm quite sensitive and so I didn't want to take anything home. So, I kind of used Curry as a mirror where I put full trust in him'. Elsewhere: 'at the end of the day it is his vision', and on a disputed memory, 'if that's what Curry said, then that's definitely what happened.'
claims.inference: Borrowing certainty from a trusted authority to manage sensitivity. It counts against a Type 4 reading (4s tend to guard their own expressive truth against the group's view) and fits 6.
claims.alternative: Normal actor-director deference on an auteur's passion project; also fits a Type 9 merging reading. Barker credits her with original ideas (S16), so the deference is not total.

claims.claim: To decompress she relies on things she can control: 'whenever it comes to what I do have control over in order to keep myself secure... it'll be my drives. It'll be my music. It'll be my video games', plus years of watching Trixie and Katya as a staple that 'brings yourself back'.
claims.inference: An explicit security vocabulary: she regulates emotions by returning to reliable, controllable rituals. Distinguish this from the role's theme of loss of control; this is about her own life.
claims.alternative: Healthy, generic self-care; many types use routines. The word 'secure' is the discriminating part.

claims.claim: On Oscar buzz she keeps 'a safety net': if a nomination doesn't happen, 'it doesn't mean that I didn't do a good job', and the conversation itself is 'more than enough'.
claims.inference: Pre-committing against a feared disappointment before it happens, the same anticipatory structure as the Twitch deletion (C15). She also admits the buzz is 'extremely validating' (S11 32:02-32:15).
claims.alternative: Media-trained modesty about awards is universal; weak alone.

claims.claim: She says she is 'very private', in 2021 and again in 2026. She copes with strangers filming her by treating it as 'none of my business' and deliberately not attending to it, and stays off social media partly to protect her acting.
claims.inference: Privacy is one of the few traits documented across time (2021 to 2026). The 'neglect it' strategy is a controlled narrowing of attention.
claims.alternative: Privacy is not type-specific (also common in 4, 5, 9) and is sensible for a newly famous 25-year-old.

claims.claim: After Obsession she said she wants to be 'very discerning' about her next projects so as not to 'lose the audience's trust'. She also wants to 'prove that Obsession wasn't just lightning in a bottle' while being willing to 'fall on my face publicly and have something that people don't like [but] maybe I do.'
claims.inference: Trust is her stated currency with audiences, consistent with 6. The fall-on-my-face line cuts against an image-first Type 3 and toward authenticity.
claims.alternative: The 'prove' language fits 3. The willingness to be disliked for something she loves fits 4. Both are career-strategy talk during awards season.

claims.claim: During the breakout she said 'I don't care how much I'm not sleeping, because I don't know if I'll get this opportunity again.'
claims.inference: Scarcity framing: success is treated as possibly unrepeatable, which drives overwork. Consistent with the worst-case anticipation in C15 and C25.
claims.alternative: A common first-breakout mindset; fits 3 (achievement) or 7 (seize the moment).

claims.claim: Her advice to young actors is to 'be extremely stubborn... Kind of be delusional a little bit. You have to really believe in yourself before other people will.'
claims.inference: Stubborn self-belief installed as a discipline, echoing her mother's 'not take no until no's a for sure' (S09). Counterphobic 6s often describe courage as something you decide to hold.
claims.alternative: Generic inspirational advice. Also fits 8 or 3.

claims.claim: She presents a tough, physical self-image: 'I love to think of myself as a very strong woman' (2021), asking a co-star to 'slap me harder' (2023), filming Obsession's backward walk on a torn ACL, and vomiting for real during a gag take.
claims.inference: A consistent toughness persona across 2021-2026. It sits alongside self-described shyness and sensitivity, the pairing typical of counterphobic presentation. Barker saw the same 'bro-y... sassiness' (S15).
claims.alternative: Supports Type 8 if read at face value. Against 8: she says Nikki taught her to stand up for herself (C33), and she discloses fear readily.

claims.claim: She reports impulsive thrill-seeking: skydiving and getting her nipples pierced on the same day for her 18th birthday, 'random tattoos', and says 'I don't think that far ahead.'
claims.inference: The strongest evidence for the Type 7 alternative. The skydive can be read as counterphobic proof of courage, but the same-day piercing and 'random' tattoos read as stimulation.
claims.alternative: Strongest counterevidence to Type 6. A 6 usually anticipates rather than 'not thinking far ahead'. Told on late-night TV for laughs.

claims.claim: She is testing voice acting cautiously ('I want to try something smaller to kind of test the waters') and has said she wants to write and direct.
claims.inference: Even when expanding, she stages risk small-first. That is incremental exposure rather than a leap.
claims.alternative: Standard career caution. The plans may change or not materialize.
claims.review_trigger: If a voice-acting, writing or directing credit is announced, update or remove the forward-looking framing.

claims.claim: She says acting is 'a place to hide and to be another person', and that playing Nikki showed her 'aspects that I didn't understand of myself': 'Nikki stood up for herself in so many different ways... that was something I needed to learn.'
claims.inference: She describes herself as having needed to learn assertiveness, which argues against Type 8. Hiding in a role fits sensitivity and privacy.
claims.alternative: Also fits Type 9 (finding her own voice through a role) and Type 4 (identity discovered through expression).

claims.claim: She says the Obsession script let her show 'ugliness' that she is usually told to hide ('you're constantly told, No, don't show that or don't be that or it's uncomfortable'), that she 'felt seen, I felt heard', and that Nikki was 'the first time that I felt like I wasn't part of someone else's story.'
claims.inference: Her strongest emotional-authenticity statements; the core evidence for the Type 4 alternative. For the 6 thesis the relevant element is permission: the role made showing big emotion safe.
claims.alternative: Type 4 (desire to be seen in her full emotional truth). The 'someone else's story' line is also a career statement about moving from supporting TV roles to a lead.

claims.claim: Director Curry Barker said casting Nikki was hard because actors could do the scary or the natural but not both, 'and Inde just nailed it'. He later said she brought a 'bro-y type of... sassiness' to Nikki that he 'didn't anticipate'.
claims.inference: Named director testimony from before release (September 2025) and after (May 2026). It corroborates range and a tough, casual exterior he didn't write.
claims.alternative: A director praising his lead while promoting a film; not a personality assessment.

claims.claim: Obsession originally ended with Nikki killing herself. Barker says Capstone asked for one throwaway take where she lives, and her performance in it persuaded him. She recalls the change as a same-day decision because 'she's a final girl' and 'we want to sit with her.'
claims.inference: Independent-in-voice accounts agree that her single take changed the ending but differ on who initiated the change. Attribute each version to its speaker.
claims.alternative: Accounts differ in emphasis (studio request vs creative decision). Don't flatten them into one story.

claims.claim: Obsession premiered at TIFF on September 5, 2025, opened in U.S. theaters via Focus Features on May 15, 2026, was made for a reported $750,000 (The Numbers lists $1 million), and had grossed about $510 million worldwide as of September 9, 2026.
claims.inference: Establishes the scale of the breakout. Budget figures conflict across outlets.
claims.alternative: Gross is still moving. Use 'more than $500 million' with an as-of date, or omit the precise figure.
claims.review_trigger: Re-check The Numbers/Box Office Mojo before publish; update when the theatrical run ends.

claims.claim: Before her casting she told Variety she had met X-Men director Jake Schreier and loved Mystique. In August 2026 Marvel announced her as Rogue in the X-Men film dated May 5, 2028, and she called it 'phenomenal. A huge honour. It's insane.'
claims.inference: Current career fact; not needed for the personality argument. Her pre-casting caution ('not all of them kind of turn into projects', S10 04:50-04:56) is a small consistent detail.
claims.alternative: Casting and dates can change before release.
claims.review_trigger: Re-check at production start and before the May 5, 2028 release; update if the role, title or date changes.

claims.claim: She is scheduled to make her Saturday Night Live hosting debut on the October 31, 2026 Halloween episode, with musical guest Gracie Abrams.
claims.inference: Upcoming event; not load-bearing for the thesis.
claims.alternative: Bookings can change.
claims.review_trigger: After 2026-10-31, confirm the episode aired and rephrase in the past tense, or remove.

claims.claim: She publicly identified as bisexual in a June 2020 Seventeen interview, describing her family's acceptance after a cousin came out and saying she 'will always speak out' against bullying of queer kids.
claims.inference: Her own disclosure at 19. Also shows loyalty to her cousin ('always been best friends') and a protective stance.
claims.alternative: Sensitive identity fact; use her own words and don't make it explanatory for type.

claims.claim: She has spoken about Latina representation and cultural identity, including how people pronounce names: 'There's so much in a name. And it's identity... the way that you say your name will also depend on the way that other people will react to you.'
claims.inference: Early (2020, 2022) attunement to how others react, and to identity as negotiated with others. That is compatible with vigilance about reception.
claims.alternative: A shared experience of many Latinx performers; not type-specific.

claims.claim: At a 2021 Superman & Lois screen test she wrote out the astrology signs 'from Aries all the way to Pisces' to hold her focus, and she described auditions as 'survival mode... getting it done, and then leaving and letting it go.'
claims.inference: A pre-fame example of managing pressure with a self-imposed structure. It matches the 'excuse me... ran outside and... recalibrated' strategy she describes in 2026 (S09 02:20-02:25).
claims.alternative: Idiosyncratic nerves management; not type-specific. Wording retrieved via summarizing fetch; verify.

claims.claim: In a 2021 interview she said she has 'very personally' an attachment to what her character Sarah went through, in an arc involving serious mental-health struggles.
claims.inference: Indicates personal familiarity with mental-health difficulty without specifics. Not to be used causally or to infer any diagnosis or event.
claims.alternative: Could refer to people close to her rather than herself. Omit, or quote exactly with no elaboration.

claims.claim: Her family split along genre lines: the Mexican side loves horror (an aunt, 'tia Maria', kept Chucky dolls in her bathroom and had Chucky on when Inde was about five), and the Australian side prefers board games and watched the Academy Awards.
claims.inference: A memorable, specific detail tying her fear of horror to early exposure. It also sits in tension with 'afraid of horror' (C19).
claims.alternative: Told for laughs on late-night TV; the age is a guess she checks with her mother on air ('Mom, like five?').

claims.claim: She rescued a scrawny orange cat with a broken hip, Teddy, in Venice in 2022, and fosters another cat.
claims.inference: A small caretaking detail, ironic given the film's infamous cat scene. Not load-bearing.
claims.alternative: Pet details change; keep dated if used.

claims.claim: Interpretation: her recurring move under threat is to secure against the worst case first (deleting the streams, the Oscar 'safety net', controllable rituals 'to keep myself secure'), borrow certainty from trusted people (her mother's script, Barker as 'mirror'), and then walk toward the feared thing (horror, screaming, the last-chance chemistry read). That is a counterphobic Type 6 pattern.
claims.inference: Interprets self-reports across 2021-2026 and several interview contexts. It names motive only as a hypothesis that fits repeated behavior.
claims.alternative: Type 7: novelty, reframing and 'high' language (C03, C12, C31). Type 4: sensitivity and the wish to be seen (C34). Type 3: 'prove' and 'proud' language (C27). Most evidence comes from a single four-month promotional window whose central role is about losing control.

type_hypothesis.against: Several behaviors read more naturally as Type 7: she enjoyed childhood relocation ('new story, new place'), reframed losing her series-regular role as 'Dog, you're free', skydived and got pierced on the same day at 18, gets 'random tattoos', says 'I don't think that far ahead', and describes auditions and challenges as a 'high' or 'dopamine'. Her most emotional statements (wanting to show 'ugliness', 'I felt seen, I felt heard', acting as 'a place to hide') fit Type 4. Her 'prove' and 'validating' language fits Type 3. Much of the evidence is self-report from May-September 2026 promotion, where humble-fearless framing is rewarded, and the role she is promoting is literally about losing control, which inflates control vocabulary. The Hot Ones anxiety lines are situational and their speakers are unconfirmed.
type_hypothesis.alternative_case: A Type 7 reading explains her novelty tolerance (enjoying eleven schools' worth of moves), fast positive reframes of loss, same-day stunts, breadth of interests (gaming, anime, streaming, voice acting, directing, animation), comic and irreverent talk-show persona, and the 'chasing that high' vocabulary. One fan-site snippet types her 7w8. On this reading the fear talk is a junket convention and the Twitch deletion a one-off impulse.
type_hypothesis.discriminator: What she does when a bad outcome is only possible, not yet real. A 7 reframes toward options and holds on to sources of pleasure; a 6 acts pre-emptively to secure against the worst case and borrows certainty from trusted people. Her clearest unforced case is deleting her own Twitch archive, which she loved and which had paid rent, because people might not 'take me seriously', while conceding 'it's not based on fact... I just panicked' (Variety, 2026-07-31). The same structure recurs: an Oscar 'safety net' set up before any nomination; rituals chosen 'in order to keep myself secure'; disclosing shyness to Barker and accepting a staged safe container before screaming (Collider 2026-05-16; Hot Ones 2026-09-08); 'used Curry as a mirror where I put full trust in him' (GoldDerby 2026-06-12); and, pre-fame, withholding belief in a renewal until it was 'definitive' (2023). Her 'high' is explicitly conditional on fear first ('whenever you're really scared of something... you get that high of accomplishing it'), which is counterphobic mastery rather than novelty for its own sake. Against Type 4, she subordinates her own read to the director's 'vision' and speaks of belonging (cast 'family', horror community 'I don't ever want to leave'), not of being different.
type_hypothesis.unexplained: The genuine enjoyment of constant childhood moves and the same-day skydive and piercing are not well explained by a security motive; counterphobia covers the skydive better than the piercing and 'random tattoos'. 'I don't think that far ahead' sits against typical Six anticipation. The 'boiling pot' image and her need to learn assertiveness through Nikki could indicate a Type 9 pattern of self-suppression. Lifelong privacy fits 4, 5 and 9 as well. Why a child raised with Chucky dolls became 'so deeply afraid of horror' is not explained by any source. There is little independent testimony from outside the Obsession promotional circle (no family, Superman & Lois colleagues or pre-2020 accounts), and the pre-fame record (2020-2023) is thin.
